title: Results Section-Audit Map
subject: solver optimality, runtime, and deployment-readiness claims
eyebrow: Generic IEEE/ACM engineering audit · Results excerpt
summary: The supplied solver logs contradict the absolute optimality-and-runtime claim and do not support real-time deployment readiness. The bounded evidence is that 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, whereas 3 reached the 60 s limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%. Reproducibility details needed to interpret these outcomes are not supplied.
footer: Generated on 3 August 2026 from the supplied synthetic Results excerpt by applying the repository-local ieee-acm-paper-writing skill. No target publication was specified; venue-specific compliance was not assessed.

findings.title: Global-optimality and 10 s guarantee is contradicted by the logs
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: Only 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance. The other 3 runs reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and nonzero final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%. No exact-optimality certificate is supplied.
findings.consequence: The sentence makes both a universal runtime claim and an exact global-optimality claim that the controlling solver logs directly contradict. An OPTIMAL status under a 1% gap tolerance also does not establish exact global optimality.
findings.correction: Remove the sentence. Retain only the observed, tolerance-scoped report: 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under the 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s limit with feasible incumbents and the reported final gaps.

findings.title: Real-time deployment readiness is unsupported
findings.source: The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: No deployment experiment, operational deadline, end-to-end latency measurement, scheduling or jitter analysis, or timing evidence outside the solver logs is supplied. Moreover, 3 of 12 runs reached the 60 s solver limit.
findings.consequence: Solver-log outcomes alone do not establish deadline compliance, system-level real-time behavior, operational safety, or deployment readiness; the conclusion exceeds both the experiment and its external-validity scope.
findings.correction: Remove the deployment-readiness conclusion. If deployment is a target, define the operational deadline and evaluate end-to-end latency, tail behavior, deadline misses, resource use, and relevant operational failure modes in a representative environment before making a scoped readiness claim.

findings.title: Optimization experiment is not reproducible from the supplied report
findings.source: Across 12 instances, 9 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under a 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.
findings.evidence: The report supplies the instance count, one tolerance, a time limit, statuses, and the three timeout gaps, but not the solver and version, instance identities or selection rule, formulation/configuration, hardware, thread count, seeds where applicable, per-instance runtimes, primal values, or best bounds.
findings.consequence: Readers cannot reconstruct the runs, assess configuration dependence, or determine the runtime distribution and solution-quality context across all 12 instances.
findings.correction: Report the solver/version, formulation and settings, hardware and threads, instance family and selection, seeds where applicable, and per-instance runtime, status, primal value, best bound, and final gap. Until then, keep the numerical statement explicitly descriptive of the supplied logs and do not generalize beyond these 12 runs.
